title: DataLake ingestion API returning 429s for nightly export consumers
text:

Thanks. I'll also shift the credit retraining job to start at 03:00 so it doesn't overlap with the BI refresh. Will watch tonight's run.

Change deployed Monday. Three clean nightly runs with zero 429s on export tokens. Closing this out.

title: PortfolioMgr rebalance preview grid takes 40+ seconds to render
text:

Need a fix or rollback before the next model-portfolio drift run.

Confirmed. The 6/29 refactor dropped the batching wrapper around the PricingSvc client, so each lot makes its own round trip. I'm restoring the batch call and adding a cache for intraday prices keyed by instrument.

PricingSvc latency itself looks normal on our side. p95 stayed flat during the slow windows, so this is purely call volume from PortfolioMgr. No infra change needed.

Fix deployed to prod this afternoon. Large-household preview now renders in about 3 seconds in my testing. Asking the wealth team to confirm tomorrow morning before we close this.

title: Equity desk VaR limit breach flagged by RiskEngine on tech basket

title: Remote staff intermittently dropped from VPN after AuthSSO token refresh
text:
[ITOPS-301] Remote staff intermittently dropped from VPN after AuthSSO token refresh
Status: resolved | Priority: P2 | Reporter: Kevin Zhao | Assignee: Barbara Beard

Multiple people working remotely report that the VPN client disconnects roughly every 55-60 minutes and prompts for re-authentication. It appears to line up with the AuthSSO access token refresh interval. Reconnecting works but kills long-running SSH sessions and database tunnels. Reported by at least six engineers and two people on the trading desk this week. Affects the Mac client version 5.2 and Windows 5.1 alike. Suspect the SAML assertion lifetime on the VPN concentrator is shorter than the session lifetime configured in the identity provider. Need to align the two settings and verify with a test group.

--- Comment by Barbara Beard ---
Found it. The concentrator was set to a 3600s assertion validity with no clock skew tolerance, while AuthSSO rotates signing context at 3300s for some groups. I'm adding a 5 minute skew allowance and extending validity to 8h.

--- Comment by Sam Okafor ---
Please roll it out to the pilot group first and get confirmation from the desk before pushing to everyone.

--- Comment by Kevin Zhao ---
Pilot group of five has been stable for two full days, no drops. Looks good to me.

title: Assess digital-asset client onboarding risk (OFS guidance)
text:
[COMP-112] Assess digital-asset client onboarding risk (OFS guidance)
Status: resolved | Priority: P3 | Reporter: Marcus Bell | Assignee: Nadia Petrov

On Jul 28, the Office of Financial Supervision sent us a letter (cc Catherine) about its interim guidance on onboarding clients with digital-asset-derived wealth. OFS expects three things:
- AML controls that can trace on-chain flows
- documented due diligence on crypto custodians
- source-of-funds verification that holds up to examiner review

OFS wants a written risk assessment by 2026-08-29.

Nadia, please assess the following:
1. Whether AMLMonitor, FraudScore and SanctionsScreen can meet the on-chain tracing expectation today.
2. What blockchain analytics tooling or vendors we have, if any.
3. Our current exposure: how many wealth prospects and clients have crypto-derived wealth.
4. Your recommendation on whether we keep onboarding these clients while gaps exist.

I'd like findings in hand before the #crypto-policy working group gets going. I'll draft the OFS response from this ticket.

--- Comment by Nadia Petrov ---
Initial findings on controls.

AMLMonitor cannot trace on-chain flows. It monitors fiat activity sourced from DataLake and scored by FraudScore. It has no wallet or address data model and no ingestion of blockchain data. When a client wires in proceeds from an exchange, all we see is the wire from the exchange's bank. Anything upstream of that is invisible to us.

SanctionsScreen screens names and entities against OFAC and other lists. It does not screen wallet addresses, even though OFAC publishes those on the SDN list.

We have no blockchain analytics vendor in place. There is no contract and no pilot. Procurement has no record of an evaluation either.

Today, source of funds for these clients rests on two things: exchange statements and client-provided wallet screenshots. Both are documents we cannot independently verify.

--- Comment by Nadia Petrov ---
Exposure. I worked through ClientHub notes and KYCPipeline cases with the Wealth Management client associates. There are 9 current wealth prospects whose wealth is substantially crypto-derived: early holders, token-project founders, and a couple of mining-related liquidity events. None are fully onboarded yet. Several are sitting in EDD review in KYCPipeline.

Custody: at least four of the 9 hold assets with third-party crypto custodians. We have done no due diligence on any of those custodians.

--- Comment by Nadia Petrov ---
My recommendation is to pause new digital-asset client onboarding until both of these are true:
(a) a blockchain analytics tool is integrated into AMLMonitor, with alerting on wallet risk and address screening wired into SanctionsScreen;
(b) OFS publishes its final guidance.

Enhanced due diligence on its own does not close the gap. Without on-chain visibility we cannot evidence source of funds, and that is exactly what OFS says examiners will test.

For the 9 prospects, I suggest we hold the KYCPipeline cases in their current state rather than decline outright. Relationship managers can then tell clients the delay is a process matter.

Marking this resolved from the assessment side. Implementing any pause is a policy decision for the working group.

--- Comment by Marcus Bell ---
Thanks Nadia, this is what I needed. I'll use these findings for the OFS risk assessment and take the pause recommendation to #crypto-policy. Resolving.

title: SEV1: PricingSvc serving stale prices (MarketDataFeed outage)
text:
[INC-0814] SEV1: PricingSvc serving stale prices (MarketDataFeed outage)
Status: resolved | Priority: P1 | Reporter: Leo Martinez | Assignee: Leo Martinez

Severity: SEV1
Status: Resolved
Incident Commander: Leo Martinez
Systems: MarketDataFeed (root), PricingSvc, RiskEngine, OMS, TradeBlotter, PortfolioMgr, SettlementEngine, ReconLegacy, ReportingBI

Summary
At 09:31 ET on 2026-08-14, MarketDataFeed lost its primary vendor connection. The TLS certificate on that connection had expired, so the handshake failed. PricingSvc did not alert because staleness flagging is suppressed while it serves from last-good cache. It kept returning prices frozen as of 09:31. At 13:31 the 4h hard TTL on that cache expired. From about 13:35, downstream consumers began failing or rejecting outright. Service was restored at 17:15 after the vendor renewed the certificate. Customer-facing impact window: 3h40m (13:35 to 17:15). Prices were stale from 09:31.

Impact
- RiskEngine: intraday VaR and exposure calculations were computed on stale prices. Risk could not monitor limits for the duration.
- OMS: pre-trade price-tolerance checks rejected orders once PricingSvc marked prices invalid. The desk could not reliably route.
- TradeBlotter: P&L was frozen at 09:31 marks.
- PortfolioMgr: scheduled wealth rebalancing runs were halted. No rebalance orders were generated.
- SettlementEngine (Sat 2026-08-15 morning): the batch was delayed while backfilled prices were validated.
- ReconLegacy (Sat 2026-08-15 morning): the EOD run produced valuation breaks on positions marked with stale prices. Operations cleared them after the rerun.
- ReportingBI: management risk dashboards showed incorrect exposures. They pulled RiskEngine output computed on stale prices between 09:31 and the backfill.

Root Cause
The client TLS certificate used on the MarketDataFeed connection to the primary market data vendor expired at 09:31 ET. The certificate was vendor-issued and outside our cert-manager inventory, so there was no renewal alert. MarketDataFeed retried the handshake in a loop without escalating. PricingSvc cache fallback masked the failure for four hours.

Follow-ups
- Add all vendor-issued certs to the cert inventory, with 30/14/7-day expiry alerts. Owner: Technology.
- Stop suppressing PricingSvc staleness flags in cache-fallback mode. Page when any instrument class is older than 5 minutes during market hours.
- Alert MarketDataFeed when handshake failures persist beyond 2 minutes.
- Add a staleness banner to ReportingBI when RiskEngine inputs are flagged stale.
- Postmortem review scheduled for week of 2026-08-17.

--- Comment by Leo Martinez ---
Timeline (all ET, 2026-08-14):
09:31 Vendor TLS cert expires. MarketDataFeed handshake starts failing and retrying silently. PricingSvc switches to last-good cache.
13:31 PricingSvc cache hard TTL hits. Prices are marked invalid.
13:35 OMS begins rejecting orders on price checks. TradeBlotter P&L shows frozen marks.
13:47 SEV1 declared in #incidents.
13:52 INC-0814 opened. Bridge started with Omar Brown and Barbara Beard (SRE).

--- Comment by Leo Martinez ---
14:05 Omar found TLS handshake errors (certificate expired) in the MarketDataFeed connector logs for the primary vendor session.
14:12 Vendor support ticket opened, requesting emergency cert reissue. Their ETA is 2-3 hours because a manual signing step is needed on their side.
14:20 Ops (Ravi Patel) flagged risk to the SettlementEngine batch and the next ReconLegacy run if prices are not backfilled.
14:40 Evaluated failing over to the secondary vendor. Rejected because it covers only part of the equity universe and none of the fixed income, so OMS would still reject most flow. Desk switched to manual voice/broker execution under Daniel Reyes.

--- Comment by Leo Martinez ---
16:58 Vendor delivered the renewed certificate. Installed on the MarketDataFeed connector after Barbara verified the chain.
17:06 Handshake succeeded and live ticks are flowing. PricingSvc cache invalidated and repopulated.
17:15 PricingSvc fresh across all instrument classes. OMS price checks passing, TradeBlotter P&L live again, RiskEngine VaR recomputing. Incident mitigated. Kicked off the price backfill from 09:31 using vendor historical snapshots.

--- Comment by Leo Martinez ---
Sat 2026-08-15 update: backfill finished at 02:40. SettlementEngine batch started about 90 minutes late while Ops validated backfilled marks. The ReconLegacy EOD run flagged valuation breaks on positions marked during the stale window. Tasha Greene confirmed these cleared on rerun against corrected prices. ReportingBI exposure dashboards were wrong until RiskEngine reprocessed Friday intraday. They are correct as of 09:10 Saturday, and Owen Gallagher's team has signed off.

--- Comment by Leo Martinez ---

title: ReconLegacy: migrate off Oracle 11g (extended support ending)
text:
[ITOPS-262] ReconLegacy: migrate off Oracle 11g (extended support ending)
Status: open | Priority: P3 | Reporter: Sam Okafor | Assignee: Priya Raman

Summary: The Oracle 11g host underneath ReconLegacy is running on extended support that is ending. We need a plan to move the nightly reconciliation batch off 11g before we are on an unsupported database with no patches. That is not a position I want to defend in an audit.

Background:
- ReconLegacy is Perl batch jobs on the Oracle 11g host. Cron kicks off at 02:15 ET.
- It reads SettlementEngine extracts and GLCore balances and posts the break report to #recon by 06:30.
- It has failed three times since July: the late FX rate table on 07-22, the stale-price abort after the PricingSvc incident on 08-14, and the tablespace failure on 08-27. Each one needed a manual intervention.

Scope (initial):
1. Inventory all Perl modules, cron entries, and Oracle objects (tables, packages, housekeeping jobs).
2. Pick a target. Options are a supported Oracle version as a lift-and-shift, or a rewrite onto the platform we already run for SettlementEngine and GLCore.
3. Run old and new side by side, comparing break reports for at least one full month-end.
4. Cut over and decommission the 11g host.

Asking Priya to own the estimate and the technical plan. Please flag anything that changes the shape of this.

Priority: High
Assignee: Priya Raman

--- Comment by Priya Raman ---
Thanks Sam. Some honest context before anyone puts dates on a slide.

The Oracle side is the easy part. The hard part is the Perl. Most modules are straightforward extract/match/report code. The FX adjustment module (step 4) is different. It holds years of special cases: how we treat same-day FX on settlement versus trade date, rounding tolerances by currency pair, and a fallback for when the PricingSvc snapshot lands late. Very little of it is written down anywhere except in the code and in my head. The same is true, to a lesser degree, of the month-end handling and the housekeeping scripts that keep the tablespace from filling up (the 08-27 failure).

Realistic estimate: about 3 months for a migration with a proper parallel run. That assumes no surprises, and there are always surprises with this code.

My strong recommendation is to pair someone with me before any migration work starts. Ideally that person sits with me on the nightly support rotation for a few weeks. They should learn why the code behaves the way it does, not just what it does. Otherwise we risk porting the bugs and losing the fixes.

--- Comment by Priya Raman ---
Adding one item for the inventory. The --asof re-run path I used on 08-15 needs to be preserved in whatever we build. Ops relies on it whenever upstream pricing is late.
